Now $\frac{{S}_{4n}}{{S}_{2n}} = \frac{\frac{4n}{2}\left(2a + \left(4n - 1\right)d\right)}{\frac{2n}{2}\left(2a + \left(2n - 1\right)d\right)} = \frac{2\left(2a + \left(n - 1\right)d + 3nd\right)}{\left(2a + \left(n - 1\right)d + nd\right)} = \frac{6nd}{nd} = 6$

questions.question: Let ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}...$ be an $A.P.$ with ${a}_{6} = 2.$ Then, the common difference of this $A.P.,$ which maximise the product ${a}_{1} \cdot {a}_{4} \cdot {a}_{5},$is :
questions.explanation:
Let, the first term of $A.P.$ be $a$ and common difference $d,$ then we know that the ${n}^{th}$term of the $A.P.$ is $a + \left(n - 1\right)d.$

Then ${a}_{6} = a + 5d = 2 a = 2 - 5d...\left(i\right)$

Let $\Delta = {a}_{1} \cdot {a}_{4} \cdot {a}_{5} \implies \Delta = a \cdot (a + 3d) \cdot (a + 4d)$

Put the value of $a$ from equation $\left(i\right), \implies \Delta = \left(2 - 5d\right) \cdot (2 - 5d + 3d) \cdot (2 - 5d + 4d) \implies \Delta = \left(2 - 5d\right) \cdot (2 - 2d) \cdot (2 - d) \implies \Delta = - 2(5{d}^{3} - 17{d}^{2} + 16d - 4)$

For finding the maximum or minimum value of $\Delta \implies \frac{d \Delta }{dd} = - 2(15{d}^{2} - 34d + 16) \implies \frac{d \Delta }{dd} = - 2\left(5d - 8\right)(3d - 2)$

Now, $\frac{d \Delta }{dd} = 0 \implies - 2\left(5d - 8\right)(3d - 2) = 0 \implies d = \frac{8}{5}$ or $d = \frac{2}{3}$

And, $\frac{{d}^{2} \Delta }{d{d}^{2}} = - 2(30d - 34)$

At $d = \frac{8}{5},\frac{{d}^{2} \Delta }{d{d}^{2}} = - 2\left(30 \times \frac{8}{5} - 34\right) = - 28 < 0$ and at $d = \frac{2}{3},\frac{{d}^{2} \Delta }{d{d}^{2}} = - 2\left(30 \times \frac{2}{3} - 34\right) = 28 > 0$

We know that if at any point the first derivative of a function is zero and the second derivative is negative, then it is the point of maxima of the function.

Hence, it is clear that $\Delta$ is maximum when $d = \frac{8}{5}.$

We know that, the ${n}^{th}$ term of a $G.P.$ with first term $a$ and common ratio $r$ is ${t}_{n} = a{r}^{n - 1}.$

Then, $b = ar$ and $c = a{r}^{2}$

Now, $3a,7b$ and $15c$ are in $A.P. \implies 14b = 3a + 15c \implies 14\left(ar\right) = 3a + 15(a{r}^{2}) \implies 14r = 3 + 15{r}^{2} \implies 15{r}^{2} - 14r + 3 = 0 \implies \left(3r - 1\right)\left(5r - 3\right) = 0 \implies r = \frac{1}{3}$ or $r = \frac{3}{5}$

The only acceptable value is $r = \frac{1}{3},$ because $r \in \left(0,\frac{1}{2}\right) ∴$ the first term of the $A.P.$ is $A = 3a$ and the common difference is $d = 7b - 3a = 7ar - 3a = \frac{7}{3}a - 3a = - \frac{2}{3}a$

Also, we know that the ${n}^{th}$ term of an $A.P.$ with first term $A$ and common difference $d$ is ${T}_{n} = A + \left(n - 1\right)d ∴{T}_{4} = 3a + \left(4 - 1\right)\left( - \frac{2}{3}a\right) = 3a - 2a = a.$
